flatline_protocol:
  enabled: true
  auto_trigger: true
  phases:
    prd: true
    sdd: true
    sprint: true
  models:
    # 2026-10-01: claude-headless = Fable 5.1 on the CLI/Bedrock; `opus`/`fable` are http_api ids that fail
    # INVALID_CONFIG without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (fleet-measured, search 2026-10-01). Was opus.
    # Flatline runs its voices in parallel and nothing serialises CLI hops across it (the per-binary lock is
    # adversarial-review.sh's): two claude -p calls share the CLI and the plan window, each bounded by the catalog's
    # headless_timeout_seconds (900 s) — up to ~15 min per phase under contention (KF-037 / KF-038).
    # Its auth follows CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN (the claude-bedrock wrapper for Bedrock, else the plain CLI's own login — bd-swz7), and it
    # shares the anthropic headless circuit breaker with the dissent companion: a rate limit on either opens it for both.
    # (thirty-seventh run, e2b DISS-C-002) so a Flatline rate limit leaves a review that follows while the breaker is open
    # single-voice: its companion is refused by the open breaker, the envelope reads companion_voice.status failed (not degraded),
    # and nothing in the unattended harness re-runs it (KF-038) — read companion_voice before taking such a review as two-voice.
    # (thirty-ninth run, e2b DISS-C-002/003) the route — and the account billed — is the environment's, not this file's: a shell
    # without CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN (cron, CI, a fresh login) runs Flatline and Bridgebuilder on the plain CLI's plan, and the breaker
    # bucket is anthropic/headless whatever the route, so a plan-window limit there also refuses a Bedrock-wrapped companion; export
    # the wrapper in every shell that runs them, and clear a bucket opened on the other route with `cheval --reset-breaker anthropic:headless`.
    primary: claude-headless
    # cycle-109 substrate-debug (2026-05-13): switched secondary from gpt-5.5-pro
    # to gpt-5.5 (non-pro). Direct probe of current OpenAI key showed it lacks
    # Pro-tier access (gpt-5.5-pro → 404 "not a chat model" on /v1/chat/completions
    # AND insufficient_quota on /v1/responses; gpt-5.5 → success with correct
    # params). gpt-5.5 is the cost-safe default per cycle-095 Sprint 2; alias
    # already in substrate catalog. Filed as cycle-109 evidence (C109.OP-6):
    # substrate misdiagnosed model-tier-access-denied as insufficient_quota —
    # FR-1 capability-aware substrate would have caught this at boot.
    secondary: gpt-5.5
    # cycle-124 (2026-09-17): tertiary DISABLED on this host — gemini CLI is tier-blocked (KF-018, rec 2) and
    # hounfour.headless.mode cli-only never reaches the HTTP rung, so a configured tertiary only turns every
    # Flatline run into 2/3 DEGRADED (Phase 2 skipped). Fleet baseline (framework-review §10): no tertiary
    # unless `agy` is installed. Re-enable by restoring the line below.
    # tertiary: gemini-3.1-pro # cheval bare-alias (resolves to API id gemini-3.1-pro-preview); was gemini-3.1-pro-preview which is not a valid cheval alias — see cycle-102 flatline-prd-degradation.md
  thresholds:
    high_consensus: 700
    disputed_delta: 300
    low_value: 400
    blocker_skeptic: 700
  max_iterations: 5
  # Phase 2.5: Adversarial cross-model review (PR #552 enforcement gate)
  # When enabled, `/review-sprint` and `/audit-sprint` invoke a cross-model
  # dissenter (gpt-5.3-codex by default) and produce adversarial-{review,audit}.json.
  # The PreToolUse:Write hook at .claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh
  # blocks COMPLETED marker writes when enabled but the artifact is missing.
  # Emergency override: LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false.
  code_review:
    enabled: true
    # cycle-104 Sprint 2 T2.9 (2026-05-12): REVERTED to gpt-5.5-pro per
    # SDD R8. Closing evidence:
    #   (1) Architecture proof — chain_resolver populates the within-
    #       company chain `gpt-5.5-pro → gpt-5.5 → gpt-5.3-codex → codex-headless`
    #       and cheval.cmd_invoke walks it on EmptyContentError. Pinned by
    #       .claude/adapters/tests/test_chain_walk_audit_envelope.py
    #       (test_primary_empty_content_walks_to_fallback mocks the
    #       primary returning EMPTY_CONTENT and asserts walk to fallback).
    #   (2) Empirical evidence — cycle-104 sprint-2 T2.10 25-trial live
    #       replay (2026-05-12) showed KF-003 NOT REPRODUCIBLE at OpenAI
    #       across 5 sizes × 5 prompts at 30K-80K input tokens.
    # The T1B.4 workaround is no longer load-bearing. If KF-003 returns,
    # the chain absorbs it; if the chain exhausts, T2.8 voice-drop keeps
    # consensus available with the remaining voices. gpt-5.5-pro restores
    # cross-model dissent diversity per cycle-102 §G2 rationale.
    # Original cycle-102 T1B.4 swap comment retained in git history.
    model: gpt-5.5-pro
    budget_cents: 200
    timeout_seconds: 600
    # KF-011 sub-mode (c) mitigation (2026-05-17): Gemini-3.1-pro empty-content
    # on review-type prompts post cycle-109 T4.10. Adding claude-headless as a
    # 4th-line voice so quorum is reachable when Gemini is silent. KF-011
    # sub-mode (b) resolved by parser fix in d9ec8cb5; this entry covers (c).
    fallback_chain:
      - gpt-5.5
      - gemini-3.1-pro
      - claude-headless
    budget_scale: diff
    budget_cents_max: 1200
  security_audit:
    enabled: true
    # Same revert rationale as code_review (cycle-104 Sprint 2 T2.9).
    # gpt-5.5-pro restored; chain absorbs KF-003 if it returns.
    model: gpt-5.5-pro
    budget_cents: 200
    timeout_seconds: 600
    # KF-011 sub-mode (c) mitigation — same as code_review above.
    fallback_chain:
      - gpt-5.5
      - gemini-3.1-pro
      - claude-headless
    budget_scale: diff
    budget_cents_max: 1200
  secret_scanning:

+Off: AgyHeadlessAdapter refuses before any binary discovery or spawn with INVALID_CONFIG, retryable false, failure_class

+def test_bisection_rescales_the_filler_to_measured_tokens(tool, fake, monkeypatch, tmp_path):
+    """The Opus 4.7+ tokenizer counts the filler ≈1.8× heavier than the probe
+    assumes: once a step has a measured size, later steps scale the filler by
+    measured/requested so each lands on its measured target."""
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FAKE_RATIO", "1.8")

+    code, record = _run(tool, monkeypatch, tmp_path, "--max-tokens-probe", "1000000", "--budget-usd", "100")
+    assert code == 0 and record["outcome"] == "clean", record["reasons"]
+    ok, fail = record["measured_input_tokens"], record["smallest_failed_input_tokens"]
+    assert ok <= 700_000 < fail and fail - ok <= 16_000          # the tolerance is in measured tokens
+    samples = record["samples"]
+    first_measured = next(i for i, s in enumerate(samples) if s.get("measured_input_tokens"))
+    for s in samples[first_measured + 1:]:
+        got = s["size_measured"] if s["size_basis"] in ("usage", "parsed") else None   # usage, or the count a rejection states
+        assert got is not None and abs(got - s["target_measured"]) / s["target_measured"] < 0.02, s
+    assert samples[0]["tokens"] == 1_000_000 and samples[0]["target_measured"] == 1_000_000
+    # the filler actually sent shrank by ≈1/1.8 against the measured target
+    later = samples[-1]
+    assert later["tokens"] == pytest.approx(later["target_measured"] / 1.8, rel=0.03)
+    assert record["tokenizer_ratio"] == pytest.approx(1.8, rel=0.02)

+"""cycle-127 Sprint 1 Task 1.3 (FR-2 / SDD D-2.1 … D-2.3): the Opus 5.5
+catalog effort default, resolved once at the cheval chokepoint.
+
+Claude Opus 5.5's vendor effort default is `medium`, one below Opus 5's
+`high`; the catalog entry carries `params.default_effort: high` and cheval
+resolves `resolve_effort(args, entry) -> (value, source)`:
+
+    explicit --effort            -> (value, "caller")
+    entry.params.default_effort  -> (value, "catalog")
+    a CLI entry's extra.effort   -> (value, "extra")     # the headless adapter's legacy rung
+    otherwise                    -> (None,  "none")      # vendor default, nothing on the wire
+
+The catalog is not schema-validated at load, so an invalid default_effort is
+skipped with one WARN (never a crash); `effort_effective` records the wire
+value after the adapter's per-family mapping (xhigh -> high on Opus 4.6).
+
+The entry is the RESOLVED one (`opus` -> claude-opus-5-5). Both adapters keep
+their contracts: the HTTP adapter emits `output_config.effort` for
+`request.effort`, the CLI adapter passes `--effort` first; the MODELINV
+envelope records `effort_source` next to `effort`; `--dry-run` reports both
+and prints `effort: high (catalog default)` / `effort: low (caller)`.
+"""

+"""cycle-127 FR-1 — the agy (Antigravity) headless route is opt-in, default off.
+
+`hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in` (a YAML boolean in .loa.config.yaml, default false) is read through the project-config layer.
+Off: AgyHeadlessAdapter refuses before any binary discovery or spawn with INVALID_CONFIG, retryable false, failure_class
+opt_in_required, naming the key and the reason. On: today's path (discovery, the one-time argv WARN, dispatch).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
+
+import pytest
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
+
+from loa_cheval.config.loader import agy_opt_in_enabled
+from loa_cheval.providers import get_adapter
+from loa_cheval.types import AgyOptInRequiredError, ConfigError, ModelConfig, ProviderConfig, CompletionRequest
+
+_MOD = "loa_cheval.providers.agy_headless_adapter"
+_REFUSAL = ("agy headless route is opt-in: set hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in: true (the prompt travels on the CLI's argv, "
+            "readable by local users; the CLI must be OAuth-authed)")
+
+
+def _adapter():
+    return get_adapter(ProviderConfig(
+        name="gemini-headless", type="gemini-headless", endpoint="", auth=None,
+        models={"gemini-3-pro": ModelConfig(context_window=1048576, extra={"cli_model": "Gemini 3.1 Pro (High)"})},
+    ))
+
+
+def _req():
+    return CompletionRequest(messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "review this diff"}], model="gemini-3-pro", max_tokens=200)
+
+
+def _project(tmp_path, body):
+    (tmp_path / ".claude").mkdir()
+    if body is not None:
+        (tmp_path / ".loa.config.yaml").write_text(body)
+    return str(tmp_path)
+
+
+# --- the key, read through the project-config layer -----------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("body,expected", [
+    (None, False),                                                         # no .loa.config.yaml
+    ("hounfour: {}\n", False),                                             # absent key
+    ("hounfour:\n  headless:\n    mode: prefer-api\n", False),
+    ("hounfour:\n  headless:\n    agy_opt_in: false\n", False),
+    ("hounfour:\n  headless:\n    agy_opt_in: \"true\"\n", False),         # a string is not the boolean
+    ("hounfour:\n  headless:\n    agy_opt_in: 1\n", False),
+    ("hounfour:\n  headless: on-a-string\n", False),
+    ("hounfour:\n  headless:\n    agy_opt_in: true\n", True),
+])
+def test_the_key_is_a_yaml_boolean_default_false(tmp_path, body, expected):
+    assert agy_opt_in_enabled(_project(tmp_path, body)) is expected
+
+
+def test_an_unparsable_config_reads_as_off(tmp_path):
+    assert agy_opt_in_enabled(_project(tmp_path, "hounfour: [unclosed\n")) is False
+
+
+def test_no_environment_override(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    for k in ("LOA_AGY_OPT_IN", "AGY_OPT_IN", "LOA_HOUNFOUR_HEADLESS_AGY_OPT_IN"):
+        monkeypatch.setenv(k, "true")
+    assert agy_opt_in_enabled(_project(tmp_path, "hounfour: {}\n")) is False
+
+
+def test_the_project_root_defaults_to_the_cwd_walk(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    root = _project(tmp_path, "hounfour:\n  headless:\n    agy_opt_in: true\n")
+    (tmp_path / "sub").mkdir()
+    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path / "sub")
+    assert agy_opt_in_enabled() is True
+    assert Path(root).is_dir()
+

+# --- the adapter refuses before discovery ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def test_off_refuses_before_any_discovery_or_spawn(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(f"{_MOD}.agy_opt_in_enabled", lambda *a, **k: False)
+    which, pgkill, run, ws = MagicMock(return_value="/usr/bin/agy"), MagicMock(), MagicMock(), MagicMock(return_value="/x")
+    with patch(f"{_MOD}.shutil.which", which), patch(f"{_MOD}.run_subprocess_pgkill", pgkill), \
+            patch(f"{_MOD}.subprocess.run", run), patch(f"{_MOD}.private_workspace", ws), \
+            patch(f"{_MOD}.subprocess.Popen", MagicMock(side_effect=AssertionError("spawned"))):
+        with pytest.raises(AgyOptInRequiredError) as ei:
+            _adapter().complete(_req())
+    err = ei.value
+    assert isinstance(err, ConfigError)
+    assert err.code == "INVALID_CONFIG" and err.retryable is False
+    assert err.context.get("failure_class") == "opt_in_required"
+    assert err.failure_class == "opt_in_required"
+    assert _REFUSAL in str(err)
+    which.assert_not_called(); pgkill.assert_not_called(); run.assert_not_called(); ws.assert_not_called()

+def test_off_validate_config_names_the_key(monkeypatch):

+"""cycle-127 Sprint 1 Task 1.4 (FR-3.1/3.2, SDD D-3.1/D-3.2, D-3.5…D-3.9):
+`tools/ceiling-probe-live.py --transport claude-headless`.
+
+The probe bisects the accepted input size through `${CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN:-claude}`
+with the headless adapter's own argv (`build_headless_argv`) plus
+`--effort low --max-turns 1`. An attempt is accepted only when the completed JSON
+`result` echoes the prompt's trailing needle; the accepted size is the CLI's
+measured usage. Size rejections (provider or CLI-local) bracket the bound;
+throttling / 429 / 5xx retry up to 3 attempts; anything else is `other`. Only a
+`clean` outcome writes the catalog (`operator_set`, `method: probed_headless`).
+
+No real CLI is ever spawned: CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN (or PATH) points at a recording
+fake, and the module asserts zero live spend (no `.run/model-invoke.jsonl` write).
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import os
+import stat
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import textwrap
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+import yaml
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+TOOL = ROOT / "tools" / "ceiling-probe-live.py"
+CATALOG = ROOT / ".claude" / "defaults" / "model-config.yaml"
+SCHEMA_V3 = ROOT / ".claude" / "data" / "schemas" / "model-config-v3.schema.json"
+MODELINV_LOG = ROOT / ".run" / "model-invoke.jsonl"
+
+# The filler is ≈10 tokens per 45 characters; the fake compares stdin characters.
+CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 4.5
+OVERHEAD = 3000          # the fake's "system prompt" share of the measured usage
+
+FAKE = textwrap.dedent('''\
+    #!{python}
+    import json, os, re, sys
+    if sys.argv[1:] == ["--version"]:
+        print("9.9.9 (Fake Claude)")
+        sys.exit(0)
+    data = sys.stdin.read()
+    log = os.environ["FAKE_LOG"]
+    with open(log, "a") as fh:
+        fh.write(json.dumps({{"argv": sys.argv, "stdin_chars": len(data), "tail": data[-80:],
+                             "cwd": os.getcwd(), "auto_memory": os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY")}}) + "\\n")
+    calls = sum(1 for _ in open(log))
+    m = re.search(r"code and nothing else: ([0-9a-f]{{12}})$", data)
+    needle = m.group(1) if m else "NO-NEEDLE"
+    mode = os.environ.get("FAKE_MODE", "limit")
+    limit = int(os.environ.get("FAKE_LIMIT_TOKENS", "1000000000"))     # in MEASURED tokens
+    ratio = float(os.environ.get("FAKE_RATIO", "1.0"))                 # tokenizer: measured per filler token
+    measured = int(len(data) / 4.5 * ratio) + {overhead}
+
+    def err(msg, status=None):
+        body = {{"type": "result", "is_error": True, "result": msg}}
+        if status:
+            body["api_error_status"] = status
+        print(json.dumps(body))
+        sys.exit(1)
+
+    if mode == "other":
+        err("Not logged in · Please run /login")
+    if mode == "garbage":
+        print("not json at all")
+        sys.exit(0)
+    if mode == "throttle":
+        err("API Error: ThrottlingException: Too many requests, please wait before trying again.")
+    if mode == "5xx":
+        err("API Error: 500 internal server error")
+    if mode == "flaky" and calls <= 2:
+        err("API Error: 529 overloaded")
+    if measured > limit:
+        if mode == "tpm":
+            err("API Error: 429 This request would exceed your organization's rate limit of 300,000 input tokens per minute")
+        if os.environ.get("FAKE_ORIGIN") == "cli":
+            err(f"Prompt is too long: {{measured:,}} tokens > {{limit:,}} maximum")
+        if os.environ.get("FAKE_BARE"):
+            err("API Error: 400 prompt is too long", status=400)
+        err(f"API Error: 400 prompt is too long: {{measured}} tokens > {{limit}} maximum", status=400)
+    result = "ok" if mode == "noneedle" else needle
+    body = {{"type": "result", "subtype": "success", "is_error": False, "result": result, "stop_reason": "end_turn",
+             "usage": {{"input_tokens": 5, "cache_creation_input_tokens": measured - 5,
+                       "cache_read_input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 3}}}}
+    if os.environ.get("FAKE_COST"):
+        body["total_cost_usd"] = float(os.environ["FAKE_COST"])
+    print(json.dumps(body))
+''')
+
+
+def _stat(p: Path):
+    return (p.stat().st_size, p.stat().st_mtime_ns) if p.exists() else None
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module", autouse=True)
+def _zero_live_spend():
+    """No test in this module may reach a model: the ledger cheval appends on
+    every invoke is byte-for-byte where it was."""
+    before = _stat(MODELINV_LOG)
+    yield
+    assert _stat(MODELINV_LOG) == before, ".run/model-invoke.jsonl changed — a live call escaped the fake"
+

+    sys.modules["ceiling_probe_live_cli"] = mod
+    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
+    return mod
+
+
+def _write_fake(path: Path) -> Path:
+    path.write_text(FAKE.format(python=sys.executable, overhead=OVERHEAD))
+    path.chmod(path.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IXUSR)
+    return path
+

+@pytest.fixture
+def fake(tmp_path, monkeypatch, tool):

+    for var in ("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL", "FAKE_MODE", "FAKE_LIMIT_TOKENS",
+                "FAKE_RATIO", "FAKE_BARE", "FAKE_ORIGIN", "FAKE_COST", "AWS_REGION", "ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX",
+                "CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK"):
+        monkeypatch.delenv(var, raising=False)
+    sleeps: list = []
+    monkeypatch.setattr(tool, "_SLEEP", sleeps.append)
+
+    def calls():
+        if not log.exists():
+            return []
+        return [json.loads(l) for l in log.read_text().splitlines() if l.strip()]
+
+    return {"bin": str(bin_path), "calls": calls, "dir": tmp_path, "sleeps": sleeps}

+
+def _limit(monkeypatch, tokens: int):
+    """The fake's provider limit, in MEASURED tokens (what the CLI's usage reports)."""

+def _run(tool, monkeypatch, tmp_path, *extra):
+    out = tmp_path / "record.json"
+    argv = ["ceiling-probe-live.py", "--model", "claude-opus-5-5", "--transport", "claude-headless",

+            # loa:shortcut: Opus 5's measured bound, not probed on 5.5; 180000 — rerun

375	+Claude Opus 5.5's vendor effort default is `medium`, one below Opus 5's
376	+`high`; the catalog entry carries `params.default_effort: high` and cheval
377	+resolves `resolve_effort(args, entry) -> (value, source)`:
378	+
379	+    explicit --effort            -> (value, "caller")
380	+    entry.params.default_effort  -> (value, "catalog")
381	+    a CLI entry's extra.effort   -> (value, "extra")     # the headless adapter's legacy rung
382	+    otherwise                    -> (None,  "none")      # vendor default, nothing on the wire
383	+
384	+The catalog is not schema-validated at load, so an invalid default_effort is
385	+skipped with one WARN (never a crash); `effort_effective` records the wire
386	+value after the adapter's per-family mapping (xhigh -> high on Opus 4.6).
387	+
388	+The entry is the RESOLVED one (`opus` -> claude-opus-5-5). Both adapters keep
389	+their contracts: the HTTP adapter emits `output_config.effort` for
390	+`request.effort`, the CLI adapter passes `--effort` first; the MODELINV
391	+envelope records `effort_source` next to `effort`; `--dry-run` reports both
392	+and prints `effort: high (catalog default)` / `effort: low (caller)`.

+def test_transient_classes_retry_with_backoff_and_count_every_attempt(tool, fake, monkeypatch, tmp_path):
+    _limit(monkeypatch, 250_000)
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FAKE_MODE", "flaky")       # the first two calls answer 529 overloaded
+    code, record = _run(tool, monkeypatch, tmp_path)
+    assert code == 0 and record["outcome"] == "clean"
+    top = record["samples"][0]
+    assert top["tokens"] == 400_000 and top["attempts"] == 3
+    assert fake["sleeps"] == [5, 15]
+    # three attempts at 400K are all paid for (two rejected at the requested size, one measured)
+    assert top["cost_usd"] >= 3 * 1.6 - 0.01
+    assert record["spent_usd"] == pytest.approx(sum(s["cost_usd"] for s in record["samples"]), abs=1e-3)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["throttle", "5xx"])
+def test_a_transient_class_that_persists_is_other_after_three_attempts(tool, fake, monkeypatch, tmp_path, mode):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FAKE_MODE", mode)
+    catalog = tmp_path / "model-config.yaml"
+    catalog.write_text(CATALOG.read_text())
+    code, record = _run(tool, monkeypatch, tmp_path, "--write-catalog", str(catalog))
+    assert code == 1 and record["outcome"] == "partial" and record["error"]
+    assert len(fake["calls"]()) == 3 and record["samples"][0]["attempts"] == 3
+    assert catalog.read_text() == CATALOG.read_text()
+
+
+def test_a_token_budget_429_that_persists_at_a_size_is_a_size_rejection(tool, fake, monkeypatch, tmp_path):
+    _limit(monkeypatch, 300_000)
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FAKE_MODE", "tpm")
+    code, record = _run(tool, monkeypatch, tmp_path)
+    assert code == 0, record["reasons"]
+    failed = [s for s in record["samples"] if s["kind"] == "size"]
+    assert failed and all(s["failure_class"] == "token_limit" and s["attempts"] == 3 for s in failed)
+    assert record["largest_ok_input_tokens"] < 300_000 <= record["smallest_failed_input_tokens"]
+

+def test_inconsistent_classifications_are_partial(tool):

+    assert code == 3
+    assert record["outcome"] == "partial" and any("budget" in r for r in record["reasons"])
+    assert record["spent_usd"] <= 2

+def _w(tool, text, ceiling, **kw):
+    args = dict(calibrated_at="2026-10-07T12:00:00Z", cli_model="global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5",
+                host_route="bedrock (claude-bedrock)", cli_version="2.1.292 (Claude Code)")
+    args.update(kw)
+    return tool.write_catalog_operator_set(text, "claude-opus-5-5", ceiling=ceiling, **args)

+def test_write_operator_set_changes_only_the_entry_and_replaces_the_shortcut(tool):
+    before = CATALOG.read_text()
+    if "# loa:shortcut: Opus 5's measured bound, not probed on 5.5" not in before:
+        pytest.skip("the catalog is already calibrated (the lead's probe write landed)")
+    after = _w(tool, before, 640_000)
+    b, a = yaml.safe_load(before), yaml.safe_load(after)
+    entry = a["providers"]["anthropic"]["models"]["claude-opus-5-5"]
+    assert entry["probed_ceiling"] == 640_000
+    # a calibrated entry is bounded by effective_input_ceiling (routing/ceiling.input_bound),
+    # so the measured value lands there too — otherwise the write would be inert
+    assert entry["effective_input_ceiling"] == 640_000
+    cal = entry["ceiling_calibration"]
+    assert cal["source"] == "operator_set" and cal["method"] == "probed_headless"
+    assert cal["transport"] == "claude-headless" and cal["cli_version"] == "2.1.292 (Claude Code)"
+    assert cal["cli_model"] == "global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5" and cal["measured_input_tokens"] == 640_000
+    assert cal["calibrated_at"] == "2026-10-07T12:00:00Z"
+    assert cal["sample_size"] is None and cal["stale_after_days"] == 90
+    assert cal["reprobe_trigger"].startswith("API-transport probe (tools/ceiling-probe-live.py --transport api) "
+                                             "from a host with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY;")
+    assert "through claude-headless on Bedrock (global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5) on 2026-10-07" in cal["reprobe_trigger"]
+    for prov, pv in b["providers"].items():
+        for mid, me in (pv.get("models") or {}).items():
+            if (prov, mid) != ("anthropic", "claude-opus-5-5"):
+                assert a["providers"][prov]["models"][mid] == me, (prov, mid)
+    be = b["providers"]["anthropic"]["models"]["claude-opus-5-5"]
+    for k in set(be) | set(entry):
+        if k not in ("probed_ceiling", "effective_input_ceiling", "ceiling_calibration"):
+            assert entry.get(k) == be.get(k), k
+    assert a["aliases"] == b["aliases"]
+    assert "loa:shortcut: Opus 5's measured bound" not in after
+    assert sum(1 for l in after.splitlines() if l.strip().startswith("#")) == \
+        sum(1 for l in before.splitlines() if l.strip().startswith("#")) - 1
+    prov_lines = [l for l in after.splitlines() if "cycle-127 FR-3" in l and "claude-headless" in l]
+    assert len(prov_lines) == 1 and prov_lines[0].startswith("        # ")
+    bl, al = before.splitlines(), after.splitlines()
+    start = bl.index("      claude-opus-5-5:")
+    assert bl[:start] == al[:start]
+    assert bl[bl.index("      claude-opus-5:"):] == al[al.index("      claude-opus-5:"):]

+def test_bisection_rescales_the_filler_to_measured_tokens(tool, fake, monkeypatch, tmp_path):
+    """The Opus 4.7+ tokenizer counts the filler ≈1.8× heavier than the probe
+    assumes: once a step has a measured size, later steps scale the filler by
+    measured/requested so each lands on its measured target."""
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FAKE_RATIO", "1.8")
+    _limit(monkeypatch, 700_000)
+    code, record = _run(tool, monkeypatch, tmp_path, "--max-tokens-probe", "1000000", "--budget-usd", "100")
+    assert code == 0 and record["outcome"] == "clean", record["reasons"]
+    ok, fail = record["measured_input_tokens"], record["smallest_failed_input_tokens"]
+    assert ok <= 700_000 < fail and fail - ok <= 16_000          # the tolerance is in measured tokens
+    samples = record["samples"]
+    first_measured = next(i for i, s in enumerate(samples) if s.get("measured_input_tokens"))
+    for s in samples[first_measured + 1:]:
+        got = s["size_measured"] if s["size_basis"] in ("usage", "parsed") else None   # usage, or the count a rejection states
+        assert got is not None and abs(got - s["target_measured"]) / s["target_measured"] < 0.02, s
+    assert samples[0]["tokens"] == 1_000_000 and samples[0]["target_measured"] == 1_000_000
+    # the filler actually sent shrank by ≈1/1.8 against the measured target
+    later = samples[-1]
+    assert later["tokens"] == pytest.approx(later["target_measured"] / 1.8, rel=0.03)
+    assert record["tokenizer_ratio"] == pytest.approx(1.8, rel=0.02)

+"""cycle-127 Sprint 1 Task 1.3 (FR-2 / SDD D-2.1 … D-2.3): the Opus 5.5
+catalog effort default, resolved once at the cheval chokepoint.
+
+Claude Opus 5.5's vendor effort default is `medium`, one below Opus 5's
+`high`; the catalog entry carries `params.default_effort: high` and cheval
+resolves `resolve_effort(args, entry) -> (value, source)`:
+
+    explicit --effort            -> (value, "caller")
+    entry.params.default_effort  -> (value, "catalog")
+    a CLI entry's extra.effort   -> (value, "extra")     # the headless adapter's legacy rung
+    otherwise                    -> (None,  "none")      # vendor default, nothing on the wire
+
+The catalog is not schema-validated at load, so an invalid default_effort is
+skipped with one WARN (never a crash); `effort_effective` records the wire
+value after the adapter's per-family mapping (xhigh -> high on Opus 4.6).
+
+The entry is the RESOLVED one (`opus` -> claude-opus-5-5). Both adapters keep
+their contracts: the HTTP adapter emits `output_config.effort` for
+`request.effort`, the CLI adapter passes `--effort` first; the MODELINV
+envelope records `effort_source` next to `effort`; `--dry-run` reports both
+and prints `effort: high (catalog default)` / `effort: low (caller)`.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import types
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

+from loa_cheval.types import (  # noqa: E402

+"""cycle-127 FR-3.4 guard (SDD D-3.4): the suites whose Opus 5.5 ceiling pins
+were swept to read the catalog must not grow a literal 180K back.
+
+The uncalibrated policy cap (`CEILING_CAP = 180_000`, the 4.x/5-family
+entries' bound until a probe calibrates them) is the one literal allowed, and
+it is allowed only as that named constant and in its SDD §2.1 docstring. Every
+other `180000` / `180_000` / `180,000` in these files fails this test — a
+literal there would turn red when the probe writes the measured Opus 5.5 bound.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+LITERAL = re.compile(r"(?<![\d_,])180[_,]?000(?![\d_,])")
+
+# file → the exact lines allowed to carry the literal (the policy cap, not the Opus 5.5 value)
+SWEPT = {
+    ".claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py": {
+        "CEILING_CAP = 180_000",
+        '"""SDD §2.1: ceiling = min(180000, context_window − default_max_tokens(entry)) — computed, not a constant."""',
+    },
+    "tests/unit/loa-status-providers.bats": set(),
+}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rel", sorted(SWEPT))
+def test_no_literal_opus_5_5_ceiling_in_a_swept_suite(rel):
+    path = ROOT / rel
+    assert path.is_file(), rel
+    offenders = [
+        f"{rel}:{n}: {line.strip()}"
+        for n, line in enumerate(path.read_text().splitlines(), 1)
+        if LITERAL.search(line) and line.strip() not in SWEPT[rel]
+    ]
+    assert offenders == [], "read the catalog instead of pinning the Opus 5.5 bound:\n" + "\n".join(offenders)
+
+
+def test_the_policy_cap_is_never_compared_against_the_opus_5_5_entry_directly():
+    text = (ROOT / ".claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py").read_text()
+    for line in text.splitlines():
+        if "CEILING_CAP" in line and "claude-opus-5-5" in line:
+            pytest.fail(f"CEILING_CAP pinned against claude-opus-5-5: {line.strip()}")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("line, hit", [
+    ("x == 180000", True), ("x == 180_000", True), ("probed 180,000 tokens", True),
+    ("1800000000", False), ("180_000_000", False), ("1180000", False), ("18000", False),
+])
+def test_the_guard_pattern(line, hit):
+    assert bool(LITERAL.search(line)) is hit

+_cmp_agy_chain() {  # <anthropic chain YAML list> [agy_opt_in YAML value | "absent"]
+    python3 -I - "$CONFIG_FILE" "$1" "${2:-absent}" <<'PY'

+s = s.replace("  code_review:\n    enabled: true\n", "  code_review:\n    enabled: true\n    companion_chain:\n      anthropic: " + chain + "\n", 1)
+if opt != "absent":

+open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)
+PY
+}

# Reviewer concerns — sprint-1 (PR: cycle-127 sprint-251 operator decisions)

Scope: `pr/head.diff` (45 files). Cite as `head/<path>:<line>`.

## Primary concerns (verify or refute)

1. **Bridgebuilder budget units** — `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/core/truncation.generated.ts:34` and
   `dist/core/truncation.generated.js:31` set `claude-opus-5-5.maxInput: 916000` (= 936000 − 20000). BB's maxInput is in
   estimate units (coefficient 0.25 tokens/char); the catalog ceiling 936000 is in provider-measured tokens. The PR's own

content.content:
=== DISS-001 [ADVISORY] head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/agy_headless_adapter.py:AgyHeadlessAdapter.complete:124
The default-off gate introduces a hard configuration failure inside otherwise valid Google fallback chains. When an upstream HTTP hop fails and traversal reaches gemini-headless, the new ConfigError aborts the invocation instead of treating the disabled route as unavailable.
-- failure_mode: Stock Google chains terminate with INVALID_CONFIG, masking the upstream failure. A custom chain with additional hops after gemini-headless never attempts those hops.
-- fix: Exclude non-opted-in agy hops during cheval chain construction, or explicitly handle AgyOptInRequiredError as a skipped hop while preserving the upstream failure when the chain is exhausted.

=== DISS-002 [ADVISORY] head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:providers.anthropic.models.claude-opus-5-5:495
The expanded Bridgebuilder budget mixes provider-measured tokens with character-based estimate units. The supplied calibration records approximately 1.8 times as many measured tokens for the probe filler, but the generated budget subtracts only 20000 from the measured ceiling without converting units.
-- failure_mode: A large diff containing similarly tokenized content can pass admission at approximately 900000 estimated tokens while exceeding 1.6 million measured tokens. That exceeds the model's one-million-token context window, causing the review request to fail despite passing truncation.
-- fix: Convert the measured ceiling into the estimator's units with a conservative margin, or use the model tokenizer for admission. Regenerate both source and distributed budgets and verify admission with content exhibiting the observed tokenizer ratio.

=== DISS-C-001 [BLOCKING] .claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/core/truncation.generated.ts:claude-opus-5-5.maxInput:34
The Bridgebuilder input budget is derived as catalog ceiling (936000, provider-measured tokens) minus 20000, but Bridgebuilder's maxInput is compared against a chars*0.25 estimate. The two units are not interchangeable: real diffs tokenize at roughly 3-3.5 chars/token, and the PR itself measured the probe filler at ~1.8x. A review admitted at ~900K estimated tokens can measure 1.1M-1.6M on the wire, above the 1M context window. The previous 160K budget had ~5x headroom to the window; the new budget sits at the window edge with zero margin for tokenizer skew.
-- failure_mode: Any review whose estimated size lands between roughly 600K and 916K estimate-tokens passes Bridgebuilder truncation and cheval's (also estimate-based) ceiling check, then is rejected by the provider with 400 'prompt is too long'. The primary Opus 5.5 hop fails, the chain walks to claude-opus-5 whose 180K ceiling pre-empts it, and the review degrades or aborts exactly on the large diffs the budget exists to serve.
-- fix: Derive maxInput from the measured ceiling divided by the observed tokenizer ratio (record['tokenizer_ratio'] from the probe, or a conservative 1.8), or keep the estimate-unit budget pinned to a value whose worst-case measured size stays under 1M (e.g. <=500000 estimate tokens). Add a test that maxInput * worst_case_ratio + default_max_tokens <= context_window.

=== DISS-C-002 [BLOCKING] .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/agy_headless_adapter.py:AgyHeadlessAdapter.complete:124
Every stock Google catalog chain terminates in gemini-headless, which is now the agy adapter with a default-off opt-in. On every existing deployment that has not added hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in: true, a chain walk that reaches that terminal after an upstream HTTP failure (rate limit, 5xx, ceiling) raises a non-retryable ConfigError from the fallback hop. The docstring claims planners read failure_class as 'not planned, never a failed voice', but nothing in the diff teaches the chain walk to skip a hop on failure_class == 'opt_in_required'; it only adds a new ConfigError subclass. This is a behavior change for hosts that have agy installed and previously completed via that terminal.
-- failure_mode: An invoke whose primary and intermediate hops fail transiently exits INVALID_CONFIG with the agy opt-in message, masking the real upstream error. Operators see a config refusal for a model they never asked for, and retries/alerting keyed on the upstream failure class never fire.
-- fix: In cheval's chain walk, treat a hop error carrying failure_class == 'opt_in_required' as 'hop not planned': skip it, keep the previous hop's error as the reported failure, and record the skip in MODELINV. Alternatively filter gemini-headless out of resolved fallback chains at plan time when agy_opt_in_enabled() is False, so the chain never reaches the refusal.

=== DISS-C-003 [ADVISORY] .claude/adapters/cheval.py:resolve_effort:925
Four values are produced where three are documented. If the payload schema restricts effort_source to an enum, every CLI-entry invoke that resolves via extra.effort emits a schema-invalid MODELINV record; if it does not, downstream consumers written to the documented tri-state silently mis-bucket 'extra'.
-- failure_mode: Schema validation of model-invoke-complete fails (or telemetry consumers drop/misclassify) for headless hops whose effort came from extra.effort.
-- fix: Either document and add 'extra' to the schema enum and all three comments, or collapse 'extra' into 'catalog' at the return site.

=== DISS-C-004 [ADVISORY] .claude/adapters/cheval.py:cmd_invoke:1829
Effort is resolved once against the primary (alias-followed) entry and placed on the single CompletionRequest shared by every hop. A catalog params.default_effort on the primary HTTP entry (e.g. xhigh on claude-opus-5-5) now flows unchanged to every fallback hop, including a claude-headless CLI hop where _effort_on_wire passes it straight through as --effort <level>. Before this change only an explicit --effort reached fallbacks. Conversely a fallback entry's own default_effort is never applied. effort_effective in MODELINV is recomputed from final_model_id but always with the primary's effort value.
-- failure_mode: A fallback CLI hop receives an effort level chosen for a different model family; if the CLI rejects it (or the model does not support it) the hop fails instead of completing, and MODELINV records an effort_effective the answering hop never used when its own catalog default differed.
-- fix: Resolve effort per hop (call resolve_effort with the hop's entry inside the chain walk, preferring the explicit caller value), or at minimum only propagate a catalog-sourced effort to hops of the same provider family and record the per-hop source.

=== DISS-C-005 [ADVISORY] .claude/adapters/tests/test_ceiling_probe_cli_transport.py:test_write_operator_set_changes_only_the_entry_and_replaces_the_shortcut:-
A bound measured through a different transport and account (Claude Code CLI over Bedrock) is stamped on the direct HTTP entry as operator_set with method probed_headless. The direct API path's pre-emption at 180K protected accounts with per-minute input-token limits; a calibrated bound is by policy never lowered by observation, so the 936000 figure will persist for direct-API accounts whose real ITPM is far below it.
-- failure_mode: Direct-API invocations up to ~936K tokens go on the wire and 429 against account ITPM limits (or 400 against the window after tokenizer skew) instead of being pre-empted locally; the chain walks and spend is incurred on the rejected attempt.
-- fix: Record transport-specific ceilings (e.g. a claude-headless entry or a per-transport field) rather than overwriting the HTTP entry's effective_input_ceiling, or gate the HTTP route on account_limits.itpm when it is known and keep the 180K policy cap until an API-transport probe runs.

=== DISS-C-006 [ADVISORY] .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/loader.py:agy_opt_in_enabled:122
The predicate deep-merges load_system_defaults(root) under the project config, so a headless.agy_opt_in: true in the framework-shipped System Zone defaults would opt every project in without any edit to .loa.config.yaml. The docstring says only ambient env is excluded, but the stated intent (operator's deliberate choice, argv exposure) argues for reading the project layer alone. The function also re-reads and re-parses both YAML files on every complete(), health_check() and validate_config() call.
-- failure_mode: A future defaults update (or a tampered System Zone file) silently enables the argv-exposed agy route repo-wide; each agy dispatch also pays a full catalog parse.
-- fix: Read only load_project_config(root) for this key (fail closed on exceptions as now) and memoize per project_root for the process lifetime.

=== DISS-C-007 [ADVISORY] .claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py:test_ceiling_is_the_computed_value_per_entry:147
For measured entries the expectation becomes min(entry['effective_input_ceiling'], cw - dmt), so the equality assertion reduces to eic <= cw - dmt, which the following line already checks. The test no longer verifies anything about the measured value. Similarly test_write_operator_set_changes_only_the_entry_and_replaces_the_shortcut now skips permanently against the live catalog, so the only path exercising the real catalog layout is the SYNTH copy.
-- failure_mode: A wrong or hand-edited effective_input_ceiling on a calibrated entry passes CI as long as it fits the window; the live-catalog writer path has no regression coverage.
-- fix: For measured entries assert effective_input_ceiling == min(measured_input_tokens, cw - dmt) and probed_ceiling == effective_input_ceiling; replace the skip with a fixture that resets the live entry to its pre-probe shape before exercising the writer.

=== DISS-C-008 [ADVISORY] .claude/adapters/cheval.py:resolve_effort:909
The 'sets both' WARN fires whenever params.default_effort and extra.effort coexist, including HTTP entries where extra.effort is never consulted by any adapter (the docstring says so). It also fires when the caller passed an explicit --effort, where neither catalog value is used. The catalog check is strict (no normalization) while the extra path lower-cases and strips, so 'High' is rejected in params but accepted in extra.
-- failure_mode: Spurious config-smell warnings on valid HTTP entries, and inconsistent acceptance of the same spelling across the two rungs.
-- fix: Only warn when _is_cli_entry(entry) and no explicit effort was given; apply the same str().strip().lower() normalization to params.default_effort before validating.

=== DISS-C-009 [ADVISORY] tools/ceiling-probe-live.py:_run_capped:-
With ANTHROPIC_API_KEY present in the operator's shell, the Claude Code CLI will authenticate with the key and route to the direct API, while the probe records host_route and cli_model as Bedrock/subscription from the wrapper env variables it inspects. The written reprobe_trigger and provenance line then describe a transport the measurement never used, and the spend lands on the API key rather than the subscription.
-- failure_mode: Catalog provenance for an operator_set bound is wrong, and the budget guard underestimates real cost.
-- fix: Spawn the CLI with build_headless_subprocess_env() (as the adapter does) plus the probe's own additions, and refuse or warn when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set while --transport claude-headless is selected.

=== DISS-C-010 [ADVISORY] .claude/adapters/tests/test_ceiling_probe_cli_transport.py:test_the_write_clamps_to_the_i2_invariant_and_keeps_the_raw_measurement:-
The v3 schema's human-readable contract for measured_input_tokens contradicts the fr23b clamp the writer now applies. Tooling or operators following the schema text will expect probed_ceiling == measured_input_tokens and read the shipped catalog entry (and any future clamped write) as corrupt or hand-edited.
-- failure_mode: Catalog consumers that validate the measured/probed relationship per the schema description reject or mis-handle clamped entries.
-- fix: Update the schema description to 'the raw accepted size; probed_ceiling and effective_input_ceiling are min(this, context_window - default_max_tokens)', and add a schema-level or loader-level check for that relationship.

The direct API path's pre-emption at 180K protected accounts with per-minute input-token limits; a calibrated bound is by policy never lowered by observation, so the 936000 figure will persist for direct-API accounts whose real ITPM is far below it.
-- failure_mode: Direct-API invocations up to ~936K tokens go on the wire and 429 against account ITPM limits (or 400 against the window after tokenizer skew) instead of being pre-empted locally; the chain walks and spend is incurred on the rejected attempt.
-- fix: Record transport-specific ceilings (e.g. a claude-headless entry or a per-transport field) rather than overwriting the HTTP entry's effective_input_ceiling, or gate the HTTP route on account_limits.itpm when it is known and keep the 180K policy cap until an API-transport probe runs.

=== DISS-C-006 [ADVISORY] .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/loader.py:agy_opt_in_enabled:122
The predicate deep-merges load_system_defaults(root) under the project config, so a headless.agy_opt_in: true in the framework-shipped System Zone defaults would opt every project in without any edit to .loa.config.yaml. The docstring says only ambient env is excluded, but the stated intent (operator's deliberate choice, argv exposure) argues for reading the project layer alone. The function also re-reads and re-parses both YAML files on every complete(), health_check() and validate_config() call.
-- failure_mode: A future defaults update (or a tampered System Zone file) silently enables the argv-exposed agy route repo-wide; each agy dispatch also pays a full catalog parse.
-- fix: Read only load_project_config(root) for this key (fail closed on exceptions as now) and memoize per project_root for the process lifetime.

=== DISS-C-007 [ADVISORY] .claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py:test_ceiling_is_the_computed_value_per_entry:147
For measured entries the expectation becomes min(entry['effective_input_ceiling'], cw - dmt), so the equality assertion reduces to eic <= cw - dmt, which the following line already checks. The test no longer verifies anything about the measured value. Similarly test_write_operator_set_changes_only_the_entry_and_replaces_the_shortcut now skips permanently against the live catalog, so the only path exercising the real catalog layout is the SYNTH copy.
-- failure_mode: A wrong or hand-edited effective_input_ceiling on a calibrated entry passes CI as long as it fits the window; the live-catalog writer path has no regression coverage.
-- fix: For measured entries assert effective_input_ceiling == min(measured_input_tokens, cw - dmt) and probed_ceiling == effective_input_ceiling; replace the skip with a fixture that resets the live entry to its pre-probe shape before exercising the writer.

=== DISS-C-008 [ADVISORY] .claude/adapters/cheval.py:resolve_effort:909
The 'sets both' WARN fires whenever params.default_effort and extra.effort coexist, including HTTP entries where extra.effort is never consulted by any adapter (the docstring says so). It also fires when the caller passed an explicit --effort, where neither catalog value is used. The catalog check is strict (no normalization) while the extra path lower-cases and strips, so 'High' is rejected in params but accepted in extra.
-- failure_mode: Spurious config-smell warnings on valid HTTP entries, and inconsistent acceptance of the same spelling across the two rungs.
-- fix: Only warn when _is_cli_entry(entry) and no explicit effort was given; apply the same str().strip().lower() normalization to params.default_effort before validating.

=== DISS-C-009 [ADVISORY] tools/ceiling-probe-live.py:_run_capped:-
With ANTHROPIC_API_KEY present in the operator's shell, the Claude Code CLI will authenticate with the key and route to the direct API, while the probe records host_route and cli_model as Bedrock/subscription from the wrapper env variables it inspects. The written reprobe_trigger and provenance line then describe a transport the measurement never used, and the spend lands on the API key rather than the subscription.
-- failure_mode: Catalog provenance for an operator_set bound is wrong, and the budget guard underestimates real cost.
-- fix: Spawn the CLI with build_headless_subprocess_env() (as the adapter does) plus the probe's own additions, and refuse or warn when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set while --transport claude-headless is selected.

=== DISS-C-010 [ADVISORY] .claude/adapters/tests/test_ceiling_probe_cli_transport.py:test_the_write_clamps_to_the_i2_invariant_and_keeps_the_raw_measurement:-
The v3 schema's human-readable contract for measured_input_tokens contradicts the fr23b clamp the writer now applies. Tooling or operators following the schema text will expect probed_ceiling == measured_input_tokens and read the shipped catalog entry (and any future clamped write) as corrupt or hand-edited.
-- failure_mode: Catalog consumers that validate the measured/probed relationship per the schema description reject or mis-handle clamped entries.
-- fix: Update the schema description to 'the raw accepted size; probed_ceiling and effective_input_ceiling are min(this, context_window - default_max_tokens)', and add a schema-level or loader-level check for that relationship.

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (= pr/PR.md)

---

## Overall Assessment

The PR (cycle-127 sprint-251 operator decisions, 45 files) lands three operator decisions: (FR-1) the agy/`gemini-headless`
route becomes opt-in via `hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in`, read by one Python predicate plus parallel yq readers in four shell
planners and the Bridgebuilder TS pipeline; (FR-2) `claude-opus-5-5` gets `params.default_effort: high`, resolved once at
the cheval chokepoint with `effort_source` / `effort_effective` recorded in MODELINV; (FR-3) `tools/ceiling-probe-live.py`
gains a `--transport claude-headless` bisection and the catalog's Opus 5.5 ceiling is hand-written to 936,000 from a
Bedrock/CLI measurement, with the fr23b I2 clamp.

What is good: the opt-in predicate is strict (YAML boolean only, no env override, fail-closed) and the shell, TS and Python
readers agree; `build_headless_argv` is extracted without changing the adapter's argv (pinned by test); the catalog checksum
and the Bridgebuilder build manifest both match the head sources; the schema additions are enum-tight and tested; the
new test suites are thorough on the paths they cover.

What blocks: the regenerated Bridgebuilder budget for `claude-opus-5-5` (916,000) mixes units — a provider-measured
ceiling minus headroom, compared against a 4-chars-per-token estimate — which the PR's own catalog comment says
under-counts by ~1.8x, so Bridgebuilder now admits reviews that exceed the 1M window. And the opt-in refusal is a
`ConfigError` raised from inside cheval's chain walk, where ConfigError hard-aborts, so the "not planned, never a failed
voice" contract the PR documents does not hold for the one place every stock Google chain reaches the hop.

Process: the implementation report (`pr/PR.md`) carries no `## AC Verification` section, which the skill treats as an
automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED on its own. The verdict below rests on the two HIGH findings regardless.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Functionality — Bridgebuilder budget units

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/core/truncation.generated.ts:34` — `maxInput: 916000` is the measured ceiling 936,000 − 20,000 headroom, but `maxInput` is compared against Bridgebuilder's chars × 0.25 estimate; a diff admitted at ~900K estimate tokens measures ~1.4–1.6M on the wire and is rejected by the provider above the 1M window.
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/core/truncation.generated.ts:34` (also `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/dist/core/truncation.generated.js:31`, `head/docs/migration/v2.0-model-generation-floor.md:309`)
**Issue:** The catalog ceiling is in provider-measured tokens (`measured_input_tokens: 972887`, `head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:513`). The PR's own provenance comment states "the filler under-counts ~1.8x under the Opus 4.7+ tokenizer" (`head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:497`). Bridgebuilder's truncation engine estimates at coefficient 0.25 tokens/char, the same class of estimate. The previous 160,000 budget sat ~5x below the 1M window, so estimate skew was absorbed; the new budget sits at the window edge with no margin. cheval's own pre-flight (`estimate_tokens`, tiktoken/len÷3.5) is also an estimate and will not pre-empt either, so the failure surfaces as a provider 400 on exactly the large diffs the budget exists to serve, after the spend.
**Why This Matters:** Every multi-model Bridgebuilder review of a large PR on `opus` fails or degrades (the chain walks to `claude-opus-5` whose 180K ceiling then pre-empts), and the docs now advertise the broken number.
**Required Fix:** Derive `maxInput` for calibrated entries in estimate units: e.g. `floor((effective_input_ceiling − 20000) / 1.8 / 1000) × 1000` using the probe's `tokenizer_ratio` (or a conservative constant), in `scripts/gen-bb-registry.ts`; regenerate `truncation.generated.ts` and `dist/`; add a test asserting `maxInput × worst_case_ratio + default_max_tokens ≤ context_window`; correct the migration note.
**Reference:** cycle-124 FR-3 / SDD §2.1 (BB truncates below cheval's gate); cycle-126 D-1.1b (provider verdict is not walked).

### 2. Error handling — opt-in refusal inside the chain walk

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/agy_headless_adapter.py:124-125` — `complete()` raises `AgyOptInRequiredError` (a `ConfigError`, INVALID_CONFIG, exit 2); cheval's chain walk surfaces ConfigError immediately ("STATIC misconfig … hard-abort"), so a stock Google chain that walks to its `gemini-headless` terminal after an upstream HTTP failure exits INVALID_CONFIG naming the opt-in, masking the real upstream error and counting as a failed voice.
**File:** `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/agy_headless_adapter.py:124-125`; contract text at `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/types.py:503-510`
**Issue:** The docstring says `failure_class: opt_in_required` is "the machine-readable seam planners read as 'not planned', never as a failed voice". The planner-side filters (`_adv_agy_filter_chain` at `head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:2356`, `isAgyRouted`, `_tertiary_routes_to_agy`) gate only explicitly configured hops or cli-only mode. Nothing teaches cheval's walk — where every catalog `fallback_chain` ending in `gemini-headless` is traversed — to skip the hop. Scenario: Flatline tertiary `gemini-3.1-pro` under `prefer-api` is planned (FTA-2), its HTTP hop gets a 429, cheval walks to `gemini-headless`, the adapter raises INVALID_CONFIG; `_companion_failure_class` maps exit 2 to `model_unavailable` (no `opt_in_required` class exists there). The operator is told to set `agy_opt_in` for a rate limit. On hosts with agy installed this is also a silent behaviour change: hops that completed yesterday abort today.
**Why This Matters:** The FR-1 acceptance claim ("never a failed voice") is false on the chain-walk path; upstream failure classes that drive retries, breakers and alerting are hidden behind a config refusal.
**Required Fix:** Either (a) in `cmd_invoke`'s walk, catch `AgyOptInRequiredError` (or any error with `failure_class == "opt_in_required"`), record the hop as skipped in `models_failed` with that class, keep the previous hop's exception as the reported failure, and `continue`; or (b) filter `gemini-headless` out of the resolved chain at plan time when `agy_opt_in_enabled()` is false. Add a test with a two-hop chain (HTTP failure → gemini-headless) asserting the exit code and MODELINV class are the upstream's.
**Reference:** #1095 safety constraint (operator config errors never masked) — cuts both ways here: the upstream error is the one being masked.

---

## Observations

### 1. Routing — CLI/Bedrock measurement written to the HTTP entry

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:494` — `effective_input_ceiling: 936000` on the `anthropic:claude-opus-5-5` HTTP entry comes from a claude-headless/Bedrock measurement; `_lookup_max_input_tokens("anthropic", …)` now returns 936,000 for direct-API callers, and a calibrated bound is by policy never lowered by observation (LSP-5), so accounts with low ITPM lose the 180K pre-emption and 429 on the wire.
**Suggestion:** Keep the HTTP entry at the policy cap until an `--transport api` probe runs, or carry a per-transport ceiling; at minimum gate on `account_limits.itpm` when known. The `reprobe_trigger` text already admits the gap.
**Benefit:** Pre-emption stays correct for the route the entry actually describes.

### 2. Configuration — opt-in predicate reads the System Zone catalog and re-parses per call

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/loader.py:122` — `agy_opt_in_enabled` deep-merges `load_system_defaults(root)` (the whole model-config.yaml) under the project config to read one key; a `headless.agy_opt_in: true` in a shipped or tampered System-Zone catalog would opt every project in without touching `.loa.config.yaml`, contradicting "an operator's deliberate choice". It also re-parses both YAML files on every `complete()`, `health_check()` and `validate_config()`.
**Suggestion:** Read `load_project_config(root)` alone (fail closed as now) and memoize per `project_root`.
**Benefit:** The opt-in lives only where the docs say it does; no repeated 1,400-line YAML parse per dispatch.

### 3. Tooling — probe subprocess environment is not the adapter's

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/tools/ceiling-probe-live.py:217` — `_run_capped` spawns the CLI with `{**os.environ, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY: "1"}`, while the adapter uses `build_headless_subprocess_env()` which strips `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (`providers/base.py:779`). With a key in the shell the CLI may authenticate to the direct API while the record stamps `host_route`/`cli_model` as Bedrock from wrapper env vars, so the written `reprobe_trigger` and provenance describe a transport the measurement never used.
**Suggestion:** Build the env with `build_headless_subprocess_env()` plus the probe's additions; warn or refuse when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set with `--transport claude-headless`.
**Benefit:** "The probe measures the shape the adapter dispatches" (D-3.9) holds for the environment too.

### 4. Testing — assertions that now read the value under test

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py:146-147` — for measured entries `expected = min(entry["effective_input_ceiling"], cw − dmt)`, so the equality reduces to `eic ≤ cw − dmt`, which line 148 already asserts; a wrong hand-edited ceiling passes. `head/.claude/adapters/tests/test_ceiling_probe_cli_transport.py:459` skips permanently now that the live catalog is calibrated, so the live-catalog writer layout has no coverage (only the SYNTH copy).
**Suggestion:** For measured entries assert `eic == min(measured_input_tokens, cw − dmt)` and `probed_ceiling == eic`; replace the skip with a fixture that resets the live entry to its pre-probe shape.
**Benefit:** The FR-3.4 sweep keeps guarding the measured value, not just the invariant.

### 5. Complexity — SIMPLICITY[shrink]

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/tools/ceiling-probe-live.py:632-848` — `_main_cli` is 216 lines with five nested closures (`_m`, `_size`, `current_ok`, `current_fail`, `step`, `next_target`) sharing `nonlocal` state; `write_catalog_operator_set` (`:402-480`) is ~80 lines of line-level YAML surgery. Both exceed the 50-line threshold without a justification marker.
**Suggestion:** Lift the bisection state into a small class or dataclass (`samples`, `ratio`, `spent_micro`) with `step`/`next_target` as methods; split `write_catalog_operator_set` into "replace scalars", "replace calibration block", "replace provenance comment".
**Benefit:** Testable units; the tolerance/re-anchor logic becomes readable without the closure graph. net: −40 lines possible.

### 6. Documentation / consistency

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/data/schemas/model-config-v3.schema.json:306` — `measured_input_tokens` is described as "the value written to probed_ceiling / effective_input_ceiling", which the fr23b clamp contradicts (shipped entry: 972,887 vs 936,000). Update the description to "the raw accepted size; probed/effective = min(this, context_window − default_max_tokens)".
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:494` — trailing comment `# cycle-124 FR-3 (SDD §2.1): see claude-fable-5-1` is stale on a calibrated value (the writer's `_set_scalar` preserves it); `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2834` and `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/audit/modelinv.py:498` still document `effort_source` as `caller | catalog | none` while the schema and `resolve_effort` emit a fourth value, `extra`.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:509` — `method: probed_headless` on an entry the tool refused to write (its outcome was `partial`, per the comment at :496); the record is honest about `operator_set` but the method field claims the tool's method. Consider `method` absent or a note in `reprobe_trigger`.

### 7. Effort resolution edges

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:909` — the "sets both" WARN fires for HTTP entries whose `extra.effort` no adapter reads, and when an explicit `--effort` makes both rungs moot; `:921` normalises (`strip().lower()`) the extra rung but not `params.default_effort`, so `"High"` is rejected in one and accepted in the other. Warn only for CLI entries without a caller value; normalise both.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:1519` — effort is resolved once against the primary entry and rides the single `CompletionRequest` through every fallback hop; a fallback's own `default_effort` is never applied, and `effort_effective` (`:2838-2845`) is recomputed for `final_model_id` with the primary's value. Low impact today (every live Anthropic hop accepts the five levels; other providers map to None), but worth a per-hop resolve or a comment in D-2.2.

---

Review complete. Verdict trailer validated as consistent (verdict-derive exit 0).

**Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED** for sprint-1 (the PR in `pr/`). Written to `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md`, with the task brief's line-per-finding form in `review.md` at the repo root.

**Two blocking defects:**

- **Bridgebuilder budget mixes token units.** The regenerated `maxInput` for claude-opus-5-5 is the measured ceiling minus headroom, but Bridgebuilder compares it against a 4-chars-per-token estimate. The PR's own catalog comment says the tokenizer counts about 1.8x heavier, so large reviews now pass truncation and get rejected by the provider above the 1M window. The old budget had 5x headroom; the new one has none. Cited at `truncation.generated.ts:34`, also in the dist build and the migration doc.
- **The agy opt-in refusal hard-aborts cheval's chain walk.** `AgyOptInRequiredError` is a `ConfigError`, which the walk surfaces immediately. Every stock Google fallback chain ends in `gemini-headless`, so an upstream 429 becomes an INVALID_CONFIG telling the operator to set the opt-in, and the voice counts as failed. That contradicts the PR's stated "not planned, never a failed voice" contract. Cited at `agy_headless_adapter.py:124`.

**Non-blocking observations** (5 medium, 5 low): a Bedrock/CLI measurement written onto the HTTP entry's ceiling where it can never be lowered by observation, the opt-in predicate reading the System-Zone catalog and re-parsing per call, the probe spawning the CLI with the unstripped environment, two tests that now assert the value against itself or skip permanently, a 216-line function, and several stale comments and a schema description the new clamp contradicts.

**Process:** the implementation report has no AC Verification section and states no formatter, type-check or test results.

**Adversarial dissent** ran two voices (gpt-5.5-pro via codex-headless, claude-headless companion). Both of its BLOCKING findings match my two HIGHs. Zero rejected payloads. One companion claim was refuted (the schema does include the `extra` enum value) and folded into a low. Trajectory log and NOTES.md session-continuity entry are written.
